methodology: The original research topic and the generated technical specification were decomposed into atomic information units based on individual requirements, features, behaviors, and constraints. Each unit was designed to be independent, self-contained, technically specific, unambiguous, and implementable as a single requirement. This involved identifying key statements, rules, and functionalities within each document and extracting them as separate atomic units. For the original research topic, the focus was on the game rules, grid representation, and I/O signals. For the generated specification, the focus was on the combinational logic, grid addressing, boundary conditions, neighbor identification, rule application, and load functionality.
mindtraced_atomic_units: The game is played on a two-dimensional grid of cells.
Each cell is either 1 (alive) or 0 (dead).
At each time step, each cell changes state depending on how many neighbours it has.
0-1 neighbour: Cell becomes 0.
2 neighbours: Cell state does not change.
3 neighbours: Cell becomes 1.
4+ neighbours: Cell becomes 0.
The game is formulated for an infinite grid.
A 16x16 grid is used.
A 16x16 toroid is used, where the sides wrap around.
The 16x16 grid is represented by a length 256 vector.
q[15:0] is row 0, q[31:16] is row 1, etc.
load: Loads data into q at the next clock edge.
load is active high synchronous.
q: The 16x16 current state of the game, updated every clock cycle.
The game state should advance by one timestep every clock cycle.
Module has inputs clk, load, data[255:0] and output q[255:0].
The circuit simulates Conway's Game of Life.
Neighbors are defined according to Moore neighborhood, which includes the 8 adjacent cells.
spec_atomic_units: Module top_module has inputs clk, load, data[255:0] and output q[255:0].
Implements Conway's Game of Life on a 16x16 toroidal grid.
clk is a clock signal.
load is an active-high synchronous load signal.
data[255:0] is a 256-bit input vector representing the initial state of the grid.
q[255:0] is a 256-bit register representing the current state of the game.
q[15:0] represents row 0, q[31:16] represents row 1, and so on.
Combinational logic calculates the next state of each cell.
The core function is to determine the number of live neighbors for each cell.
Game of Life rules are applied to determine the next state of that cell.
Neighbor Counting: Identify eight neighbors in the toroidal grid for each cell q[i].
Wrap-around effect at the edges of the grid is considered.
Neighbor indices are calculated using modulo arithmetic.
For a cell at index i, its row is row = i / 16 and its column is col = i % 16.
Toroidal row and column indices are calculated as: row = (row + 16) % 16, col = (col + 16) % 16.
Game of Life Rules Application: next_q[i] = ( (neighbors == 2) & q[i] ) | (neighbors == 3).
Parallel Update: The next state next_q[i] is calculated for all 256 cells in parallel.
Neighbor Calculation Modules (256 instances): Each module calculates the indices of the eight neighbors.
Neighbor Summation Modules (256 instances): Each module sums the values of the eight neighbors.
Rule Application Modules (256 instances): Each module applies the Game of Life rules.
Grid Representation: 16x16 grid represented by a 256-bit vector q[255:0].
Cell Access: index i = r * 16 + c.
Toroidal Boundary Conditions: toroidal_row = (r + 16) % 16, toroidal_col = (c + 16) % 16.
Neighbor Identification: Each cell has eight neighbors (N, S, E, W, NE, NW, SE, SW).
Neighbor Counting Logic: neighbor_count = q[N] + q[S] + q[E] + q[W] + q[NE] + q[NW] + q[SE] + q[SW].
Game of Life Rules: next_state = (q[i] & (neighbor_count == 2 | neighbor_count == 3)) | (~q[i] & (neighbor_count == 3)).
Parallel Update: The next state of all 256 cells must be calculated in parallel.
Load Functionality: q[i] = load ? data[i] : next_q[i].
The `q` register is updated on the positive edge of `clk`.
When `load` is high, the value of `data` is loaded into `q` on the next positive edge of `clk`.
Otherwise, `q` is updated with the next state of the Game of Life based on the current state of `q` at every positive edge of `clk`.
